title: EndoMove – a multicenter prospective study on the effectiveness of a training program for reducing musculoskeletal pain among endoscopy staff
summary:
Background
Physicians and nurses who are involved in endoscopic procedures are exposed to particular physical strains during their work. Repetitive movements, prolonged work in fixed positions, and the exertion of force—for example, when maneuvering an endoscope—can lead to pain in the hands, neck, shoulders, or back. Studies show that such complaints are very common among endoscopists. To date, however, there is little scientific evidence regarding which measures in everyday work actually help prevent or alleviate such symptoms. In particular, there has not yet been sufficient research into whether short and easy-to-perform exercises are effective in the clinical setting and can be permanently integrated into daily routines

Research Question
The aim of this study is to examine how well the participants (physicians and nursing staff in the endoscopy unit) implement a 12-week training program and what effects the program has on musculoskeletal symptoms. In addition, the study aims to determine the level of adherence to the training program and how this changes over the course of the intervention.

Methodology
Participants complete a mild 12-week training program. During this time, health and study-related data are collected regularly through app-based questionnaires. Once a week, participants report how often they followed the training program during the previous week.

interventions.name:
The study consists of four phases: baseline (week 0), intervention (weeks 1-12), post-intervention assessment (week 12), and follow-up (week 16).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Professional experience in gastrointestinal endoscopy (medical or nursing field)
Exclusion criteria:
• Age < 18 years
• Lack of a written informed consent form for participation in the study
• Current or past musculoskeletal injury that prevents full participation in the exercise program for medical reasons
• Other medical conditions (e.g., severe heart failure) that prevent full participation in the exercise program for medical reasons
• Pregnancy/breastfeeding
